location.evidence: Top programs cluster in Massachusetts, near the nation's largest life sciences cluster, while the lowest cluster in Puerto Rico, where BLS data show wages trail the U.S. mainland in every major occupational group.

prestige.evidence: The top programs are more selective than typical biology programs, but not elite as a group. Half of them sit in Massachusetts, home to the Boston-Cambridge life sciences cluster, the largest in the nation. So both the schools and the local biotech jobs shape the top end.

stepping_stone.evidence: Biological sciences is by far the most common undergraduate major among medical school applicants and matriculants, so many biology graduates are still in training a year after college.

programs.evidence: MIT admits very few applicants, and its biology department says graduates often go on to PhD and MD programs or into drug development and other industry jobs near the Boston biotech cluster.
